home.subtitle: Drag in a PNG and get back a clean, editable, path-based SVG — traced entirely in your browser. Nothing is ever uploaded.
home.whatIsBody: A PNG is a grid of colored pixels — zoom in far enough and you'll see the blocks. An SVG is different: it stores an image as a set of mathematical paths and shapes, so it can scale to any size, from a favicon to a billboard, without ever going blurry or pixelated. Vectorization (also called "image tracing") is the process of analyzing a raster image like a PNG and reconstructing it as those scalable vector paths. That's exactly what this tool does, instantly and entirely on your device.
home.pngVsSvgHeading: PNG vs SVG at a Glance
home.pngVsSvgIntro: The short version: a PNG is fixed at whatever resolution it was saved at, while an SVG redraws itself perfectly at any size. Here's how the two formats actually compare.

faqs.question: Is this PNG to SVG converter really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every conversion is free with no limit on the number of files, no subscription, and no watermark added to your downloads.

faqs.question: Will the SVG work in Cricut Design Space or Silhouette Studio?
faqs.answer: Yes. The output is a standard path-based SVG file, which both Cricut Design Space and Silhouette Studio can import directly.

faqs.question: Can I control how many colors are in the traced SVG?
faqs.answer: Yes. Full Color mode includes a color-count slider so you can simplify a photo down to a handful of flat regions or keep a richer palette.

faqs.question: Does it preserve transparent backgrounds?
faqs.answer: Yes. If your PNG has a transparent background, that transparency is read from the alpha channel and carried through to the SVG.

faqs.question: What's the actual difference between PNG and SVG?
faqs.answer: A PNG is a fixed grid of pixels, so it gets blurry when scaled up. An SVG stores an image as mathematical paths, so it can be resized to any dimension without losing quality.

faqs.question: Can I edit the SVG after downloading it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the output is real path data, you can open it in Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma, or any vector editor and edit the shapes directly.

faqs.question: Is there a file size or file count limit?
faqs.answer: No. You can convert as many PNG files as you like, and there's no artificial size cap — very large images will simply take longer to trace.

faqs.question: Does this work well for both logos and photographs?
faqs.answer: Logos and icons with flat colors trace especially cleanly into just a few paths. Photographs work best in Full Color mode and produce a more stylized, poster-like vector result rather than a pixel-perfect copy.

faqs.question: Do you store or upload my images?
faqs.answer: No. Conversion happens entirely on your device using your browser's Canvas API — your files are never sent to a server or stored anywhere.

faqs.question: What software can open the SVG files I download?
faqs.answer: Any standard SVG file works in Adobe Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma, Affinity Designer, Cricut Design Space, Silhouette Studio, and web browsers.

faqs.question: Is this an AI-powered vectorizer?
faqs.answer: No — it uses a deterministic tracing algorithm (color quantization and edge detection), not a machine-learning model. That means the same image and settings always produce the same result, and every setting you see is one you can actually control, rather than an opaque "AI quality" toggle.

faqs.question: Can I convert JPG or WebP images too, not just PNG?
faqs.answer: This tool is focused specifically on PNG, since PNG's per-pixel transparency is central to how it handles backgrounds. If you have a JPG or WebP, converting or re-saving it as PNG first works well, especially if you don't need to preserve transparency.

about.title: About PNGtoSVG
about.p1: PNGtoSVG is a free, browser-based tool that converts PNG images into real, path-based SVG vector files. It exists to make image vectorization — turning a raster image into scalable vector paths — fast, private, and available to anyone, without a paid subscription, a required account, or a watermark on the result.
about.p2: Every conversion runs locally in your browser using the Canvas API and a background Web Worker. Your image is decoded, traced, and turned into an SVG entirely on your own device — it's never uploaded to a server, which is what lets us say the tool is 100% private by design rather than by policy.
about.p3: We built PNGtoSVG after running into the same problem repeatedly: needing a quick, reliable way to turn a logo, sketch, or icon into a clean vector file for a cutting machine, a website, or a print project, without installing design software or uploading files to yet another account-gated service.
about.whoMakersBody: Preparing designs for Cricut, Silhouette, laser cutters, and embroidery digitizing software.
about.whoDesignersBody: Turning a raster logo or icon into a scalable SVG for a website, app, or print project.
about.approachP1: We keep the tool free and unlimited because a converter that gatekeeps basic functionality behind a paywall isn't solving the problem it claims to. We keep it private because we simply don't want the liability, complexity, or user trust problem of handling anyone's image files on a server.
about.approachP2: If you'd like to understand more about how the underlying conversion works, see [how image tracing works](/guides/how-image-tracing-works), or read our [privacy policy](/privacy) for the full detail on what data (if any) we collect.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy

sections.heading: Your Images Are Never Uploaded
sections.body: PNGtoSVG converts images entirely inside your browser using the Canvas API and a background Web Worker. The PNG file you select is read, traced, and turned into an SVG on your own device — it is never sent to our servers or any third party, and we have no ability to see, store, or access the images you convert.

sections.heading: No Account Required
sections.body: You don't need to create an account or provide an email address to use the converter, so we don't collect any personal information as part of the conversion process itself.

sections.heading: Analytics
sections.body: We may use privacy-respecting, aggregate analytics (such as anonymized page-view counts) to understand overall traffic and improve the site. This data does not identify you individually, and we do not use third-party advertising trackers or sell data to advertisers.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.body: We use a single local storage entry in your browser to remember your light/dark theme preference. This stays on your device and is never transmitted to us.

sections.heading: Children's Privacy
sections.body: PNGtoSVG does not knowingly collect personal information from children, since the tool does not collect personal information from any user in the first place.

sections.heading: Changes to This Policy
sections.body: If our data practices change, we'll update this page with a new "last updated" date. Since conversion happens entirely in your browser, we don't expect this policy to change often.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about this policy can be sent to privacy@pngtosvgconverter.com.
